pool.note: Keyed by the stress type (key-guaranteed) then the NPC's role class; the role class guarantees only the NPC. wartime.mil.short/.note need 'soldiers' — data/defenceTwinLines.js reads that as garrison OR a hired company and swaps a twin where neither stands; the vocabulary has no mercenary atom, so garrison is declared (a hired-company-only place would be a false refusal). insurgency.mil.short presumes the watch specifically (no twin). mass_migration does not fix the direction, so 'the influx' needs migration: influx. slave_revolt.merchant.short presumes a market (its suspension). wartime.gov.* presumes a crown overlord (no atom).

rows.text: Satisfy the crown requisition order without stripping the settlement to the bone
The war has made every civic decision a military calculation. The crown's needs and the settlement's needs are not the same calculation.
Keep unit cohesion as conscription pulls away experienced soldiers and replaces them with frightened substitutes
Every experienced soldier conscripted into the field army is a hole in local security that a substitute won't fill the same way.
Secure a war contract before a rival does, or find a way to profit from the disruption instead of suffering it
Maintain the appearance of legitimate authority while the substance of it is actively contested
Every public appearance is a performance of control. The private meetings are about whether there is still enough control to perform.
Determine which members of the watch are loyal to the institution and which are loyal to whoever is paying them
An insurgency that has lasted this long has had time to make investments in the security apparatus.
Avoid being forced to publicly declare support for either the governing faction or the insurgency, and run out of reasons before the pressure does
Manage the influx without the old residents concluding the governing authority has chosen the newcomers over them
The governing faction is caught between two constituencies that want incompatible things, and both know it.
Either profit from the demographic change or find a way to be insulated from it. Either answer requires moving faster than the uncertainty
Establish which residents are registered, which are transient, and which are neither: before one of the third category becomes a problem
Preserve the institution's position through the transition without either abandoning the congregation or openly defying the new authority
The institution has survived political upheaval before by being indispensable. Whether it can repeat that calculation here is the open question.
Delay a public declaration on the religious question for as long as the political cost of delay is lower than the cost of choosing a side
End the revolt without either full suppression or formal negotiation: both options set precedents the governing faction cannot afford
The revolt's continued existence is itself a delegitimisation. Every day it continues is evidence that the authority is not in control.
Contain the revolt geographically without deploying force that will create martyrs and widen the conflict
The orders are to restore order. The orders do not specify what order is supposed to look like when this is over.
Recover the economic loss from the market suspension, or redirect capital away from a labour system that may not survive this in its current form
